knowledge_refs.formula_empty_justification: The nucleon number is obtained by adding the stated proton and neutron counts; this arithmetic does not apply a major reusable physics relationship.

hints: The nucleon number is the total number of protons and neutrons.
The proton number is the number of protons and identifies Sm.

ai_rubric.observable: Writes samarium as ¹⁴⁷₆₂Sm, or equivalent correctly placed nucleon and proton numbers.

hints: Look at whether the spectrum shows one kinetic energy or a spread of energies.
Alpha particles from one decay have discrete energy, whereas beta particles have a continuous range.
Use both observations to justify the radiation conclusion.
walkthrough: The spectrum is a single sharp line, so all emitted particles have one discrete kinetic energy.
This is characteristic of alpha particles.
Beta particles would produce a continuous range of kinetic energies, so the spectrum excludes beta emission.

ai_rubric.observable: Identifies the single discrete kinetic energy as evidence for alpha emission.
Explains that beta particles have a continuous range of kinetic energies and are therefore not emitted.

hints: An alpha particle has nucleon number 4 and proton number 2.
Conserve both nucleon number and proton number when finding the Nd nucleus.
Subtract the alpha numbers from the Sm numbers.
walkthrough: Conserving nucleon number gives 147 − 4 = 143, and conserving proton number gives 62 − 2 = 60.
The equation is ¹⁴⁷₆₂Sm → ¹⁴³₆₀Nd + ⁴₂α.

ai_rubric.observable: Writes the parent and daughter nuclides as ¹⁴⁷₆₂Sm and ¹⁴³₆₀Nd, respectively.
Includes the correctly notated alpha particle ⁴₂α.

knowledge_refs.formula_empty_justification: This uses recalled discrete quark charges and charge conservation, not a controlled major reusable physics formula.

hints: Up has charge +2/3e and bottom has charge −1/3e.
Add those two charges, then make the total for all three quarks equal zero.
walkthrough: The up quark contributes +2/3e and the bottom quark contributes −1/3e, so together they contribute +1/3e.
The baryon charge is zero, so 0 = +1/3e + q.
Therefore the third quark has charge q = −1/3e.

ai_rubric.observable: States the charge of an up quark as +2/3e or a bottom quark as −1/3e.
Uses zero total charge to obtain a third-quark charge of −1/3e.

hints: The third quark must have charge −1/3e.
It must also have a different flavour from the stated up and bottom quarks.
Recall which quark flavours have charge −1/3e.
walkthrough: The third quark must have charge −1/3e and cannot be bottom because all three flavours differ.
Down and strange quarks each have charge −1/3e.
Either down or strange is a possible third flavour.

ai_rubric.observable: States down or strange as a possible third-quark flavour.
